A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Neural Force Field research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–G are readable and sufficiently complete for reliable comparison.

before.justification: v3 reports original NFF prediction and planning experiments on I-PHYRE, N-body, and PHYRE, alongside ablation, robustness, timing, and GPT-4o results.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results in the main text and appendices, including Tables 1–4 and A1–A6.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Appendix B retain the same dynamic interaction graphs, DeepONet force predictor, ODE integration, MSE training, and forward/backward planning procedures.

E1.justification: The same I-PHYRE games, planetary/cometary N-body systems, and PHYRE templates are used. Within-scenario, cross-scenario, planning, and noisy-perception coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches throughout: IN, GCN, and SlotFormer in Table 1; DQN, RPIN, and SlotFormer in Table 3; and the same random, human, and GPT-4o comparisons in the planning analyses.

E3.justification: Sections 4 and Appendices A–B retain the same splits, training samples, trajectory lengths, preprocessing, model configurations, budgets, and metrics. The five-round I-PHYRE procedure with 500 action candidates also remains unchanged.

E4.justification: Both retain the ODE, neural-operator, and integration-precision ablations; integrator comparisons; noise and refinement analyses; controlled force-response plots; and prediction/encoding failure cases. No analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: SEM reporting and plotted error bars are unchanged. Both specify 20 I-PHYRE planning trials and three timing repetitions in Table A4, with no added seed information or statistical procedures.

E6.justification: All experimental entries in Tables 1–4 and A1–A6 match, as do the plotted and qualitative results. For example, NFF’s PHYRE AUCCESS remains 49.22, and GPT-4o’s cross-scenario round scores remain 0.35, 0.45, and 0.51.

T1.justification: The force-field and ODE equations, planning expressions, and Appendix B.2 metric definitions are mathematically unchanged. Differences in delimiter sizing and equation spacing are typesetting changes; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about few-shot physical learning, generalization, and planning. Adding 'GNN-based' before existing comparison methods does not alter the contribution or performance claims.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and result interpretations remain unchanged. Section 5 retains the same potential applications and limitations concerning varying friction/elasticity, deterministic rigid-body environments, and untested stochastic, soft-body, and fluid settings.

D1.justification: Appendices A–B preserve the implementation, hyperparameter, hardware, and data-processing details. The GPT-4o prompt, project link, and statement about releasing code and data after publication are also unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive research positioning remain the same. Kang et al. changes from 2024 to 2025 while retaining the same title and arXiv identifier; the GNN characterization already appears in the related-work discussion.

P1.justification: v4 expands author affiliations, renames the acknowledgments heading, changes the funding identifier from 62376031 to 62376009, and makes small wording and bibliographic edits. Appendix references change from 'Appx.' to 'Sec.'; the narrative and section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Expanded affiliations alter the title-page layout. Figure 2 is slightly resized/repositioned, with associated text wrapping and equation/caption spacing adjustments. All figures and tables retain their content and overall organization.

improvement.justification: v4 updates administrative information and lightly edits wording and layout, while retaining the same methods, empirical evidence, claims, limitations, and reproducibility information. These small editorial adjustments do not establish a meaningful net change in overall paper quality.
